result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [register_adapter()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: >- Register a contract adapter so that it can be used for import and export. twitter-card: title: >- [register_adapter()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} | Pointblank description: >- Register a contract adapter so that it can be used for import and export. title: >- [register_adapter()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Register a contract adapter so that it can be used for import and export. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Register a contract adapter so that it can be used for import and export. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/adapters/_registry.py#L11-L148){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature register_adapter(format_name=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Pointblank ships with adapters for JSON Schema, Frictionless Table Schema, dbt, and the Open Data Contract Standard, but many organizations describe their data in other ways: an in-house data dictionary, a spreadsheet export, or a schema format from another tool. Writing a [`ContractAdapter`](`pointblank.ContractAdapter`) subclass for such a format and registering it with `register_adapter()` makes the format a first-class citizen. [`import_contract()`](`pointblank.import_contract`) and [`export_contract()`](`pointblank.export_contract`) can then use it by name with `format=`, and [`list_adapters()`](`pointblank.list_adapters`) includes it. Registration creates one instance of the class (by calling it with no arguments) and stores it under the format name for the rest of the session. Registering a second adapter under a name that's already taken replaces the first one, and that includes the built-in adapters. When a format has to be detected, adapters are tried in the order they were registered, so the built-in adapters are always tried before custom ones. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [format_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The name to register the adapter under, which becomes the value to pass to `format=`. If `None` (the default), the class's own `format_name` attribute is used. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Callable or type]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : When called with a name (or with no arguments), a decorator that registers the class it's applied to and returns that class unchanged. When applied directly to a class (as a bare `@register_adapter`), the class itself, unchanged. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If no name is given and the class has an empty `format_name` attribute. ::: ## Ways To Register {.doc-ways-to-register} There are three equivalent ways to register an adapter class: - `@register_adapter("name")` above the class definition registers it under `"name"` - a bare `@register_adapter` above the class definition uses the class's `format_name` - `register_adapter("name")(AdapterClass)` registers a class that's already been defined (the name can be left out here too, as in `register_adapter()(AdapterClass)`) ## Examples {.doc-examples} Suppose a team keeps a simple list of required columns in a dictionary with a `required_columns` key. A minimal adapter for this format only needs to say how to recognize it and how to turn it into a [`ContractImport`](`pointblank.ContractImport`). Since this adapter can't export, it sets `supports_export = False`. ::: {#9544d4d5 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb from pointblank.adapters import MappedConstraint @pb.register_adapter("required_columns") class RequiredColumnsAdapter(pb.ContractAdapter): format_name = "required_columns" supports_export = False @staticmethod def detect(source): return isinstance(source, dict) and "required_columns" in source def import_contract(self, source, **kwargs): columns = source["required_columns"] return pb.ContractImport( source_format="required_columns", columns=[(col, None) for col in columns], constraints=[ MappedConstraint("col_vals_not_null", {"columns": col}, f"{col} is required") for col in columns ], ) ``` ::: The new format now appears next to the built-in ones in `list_adapters()`. ::: {#867cde43 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} for name, info in pb.list_adapters().items(): print(f"{name:<18} import={info['supports_import']} export={info['supports_export']}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` dbt import=True export=True frictionless import=True export=True json_schema import=True export=True odcs import=True export=True required_columns import=True export=False ``` ::: ::: And it can be used with `import_contract()`, either by name or (since it implements `detect()`) by letting the format be detected from the content. ::: {#39e2f926 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} imported = pb.import_contract({"required_columns": ["id", "email"]}) imported.constraints ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` [MappedConstraint('col_vals_not_null', columns='id'), MappedConstraint('col_vals_not_null', columns='email')] ``` ::: ::: Exporting to this format isn't possible, so `export_contract()` raises an error that says so. ::: {#d92c689e .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} contract = pb.Contract(name="users", steps=[pb.Step("col_vals_not_null", columns="id")]) try: pb.export_contract(contract, format="required_columns") except ValueError as e: print(e) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Adapter 'required_columns' does not support export. ``` ::: ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~ContractAdapter`) : The base class to subclass when writing an adapter. [](`~ContractImport`) : What an adapter's `import_contract()` method returns. [](`~list_adapters`) : List the registered adapters. [](`~import_contract`) : Import a definition using a registered adapter. [](`~export_contract`) : Export a contract using a registered adapter.
